facts.text: Dawson Creek takes its name from the creek surveyed by George Mercer Dawson in August 1879, who had the watercourse labeled with his name.
The town’s five wooden grain elevators, once called “Elevator Row,” were demolished in the 1970s, leaving only one converted into an art gallery.
During World War II, Dawson Creek hosted a Royal Canadian Air Force station that opened in September 1944 and operated until 1964.
Since 1959, CJDC‑TV has broadcast from Dawson Creek, shifting from a CBC affiliate to a CTV 2 affiliation in 2016.
The Peace River region was once home to nomadic Sekanni and Beaver peoples, later inhabited by Cree before European exploration in the late 1700s.
A historic general store and hotel were relocated two miles to make room for the train station that helped launch Dawson Creek’s growth.
